takeaway: Cerebellopontine angle tumours are usually acoustic neuromas, arising from the vestibulocochlear nerve at the auditory meatus.

lines.text: A forty-five-year-old woman is found to have a space-occupying lesion.
It sits at the cerebellopontine angle, between the cerebellum and the pons.
Tumours in this angle are usually acoustic neuromas.
They arise from the vestibulocochlear nerve, at the auditory meatus.
So the lesion is not coming from the cerebellum itself, even though it lies right beside it.
A lesion at the cerebellopontine angle usually arises from the vestibulocochlear nerve.
